questions.question: Which of the following organ systems jointly coordinate and integrate all the activities of the body organs so that they function in a synchronised fashion?
questions.explanation: The neural system and endocrine system work together to coordinate and integrate all the activities of the body's organs in a synchronized manner. The neural system provides fast and precise point-to-point coordination through nerve impulses, while the endocrine system provides chemical integration via hormones, ensuring long-term regulation and homeostasis.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से अंग तंत्र संयुक्त रूप से शरीर के सभी अंगों की गतिविधियों का समन्वय और एकीकरण करते हैं ताकि वे एक समकालिक तरीके से कार्य करें?

questions.question: The functions of the organs/organ systems in our body must be coordinated to maintain
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment through the coordination of organ systems.

hi.question: हमारे शरीर में अंगों/अंग प्रणालियों के कार्यों को बनाए रखने के लिए समन्वित किया जाना चाहिए

questions.question: The process through which two or more organs interact and complement the functions of one another is called
questions.explanation: Coordination is the process where two or more organs interact to function harmoniously.

hi.question: दो या अधिक अंगों के परस्पर क्रिया करने और एक दूसरे के कार्यों को पूरक करने की प्रक्रिया को कहा जाता है:

questions.question: The system responsible for providing an organised network of point to point connections for a quick coordination is called
questions.explanation: The neural system is responsible for providing an organized network of point-to-point connections, enabling quick coordination of body functions. It achieves this through nerve impulses, which are transmitted rapidly across neurons to ensure immediate responses to stimuli.

hi.question: त्वरित समन्वय के लिए बिंदु-दर-बिंदु संयोजन का एक संगठित नेटवर्क प्रदान करने के लिए जिम्मेदार तंत्र को कहा जाता है-

questions.question: The neural system is better organised in ____A____ where a brain is present along with a number of ____B____and ____C____.
options: Insect, ganglia and neural tissues, respectively
Hydra, neural tissues and ganglia, respectively
questions.explanation: Insects have a better-organized neural system with a brain, ganglia, and neural tissues. Hydra lacks a brain but has a nerve net instead. Vertebrates have a brain but do not rely on ganglia for coordination.

hi.question: तंत्रिका तंत्र A में बेहतर रूप से व्यवस्थित होता है जहाँ एक मस्तिष्क B और C की संख्या के साथ मौजूद होता है।

questions.question: Which of the following system provides the fastest means of communication within the body?
questions.explanation: The nervous system provides the fastest means of communication via electrical impulses.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी प्रणाली शरीर के भीतर संचार का सबसे तेज़ साधन प्रदान करती है?

questions.question: Endocrine system provides chemical integration through:
questions.explanation: (1) The endocrine system regulates body functions through hormones, which act as chemical messengers. [New NCERT Class 11th Page no. 239]

hi.question: अंतःस्रावी तंत्र रासायनिक एकीकरण प्रदान करता है:

questions.question: The neural system of all animals is composed of highly specialised cells called
questions.explanation: The neural system of all animals is composed of highly specialized cells called neurons. These cells are responsible for detecting, receiving, and transmitting different kinds of stimuli. Neurons are the structural and functional units of the nervous system.

hi.question: सभी जन्तुओं का तंत्रिका तंत्र अत्यधिक विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं से मिलकर बना होता है, जो कहलाती है:
hi.explanation: सभी जानवरों का तंत्रिका तंत्र अत्यधिक विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं से बना होता है जिन्हें न्यूरॉन्स कहा जाता है। ये कोशिकाएँ विभिन्न प्रकार की उत्तेजनाओं का पता लगाने, उन्हें प्राप्त करने और संचारित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार होती हैं। न्यूरॉन्स तंत्रिका तंत्र की संरचनात्मक और कार्यात्मक इकाइयाँ हैं।

questions.question: Neurons are specialised cells for
questions.explanation: Neurons are specialized cells that are responsible for the conduction of nerve impulses. They receive, process, and transmit information through electrical and chemical signals, facilitating communication between different parts of the body.

hi.question: न्यूरॉन विशिष्ट कोशिकाएँ हैं-
options: तंत्रिका आवेगों के चालन के लिए

questions.question: Neurons can
questions.explanation: Neurons are specialized cells that detect, receive, and transmit stimuli in the form of electrical and chemical signals. They play a crucial role in the neural system by ensuring rapid communication between different parts of the body.

hi.question: न्यूरॉन्स का कार्य हैं-

questions.question: Basic functions of neural system is/are
options: Receiving sensory input from internal and external environment by nerves
questions.explanation: The neural system performs the following basic functions: Receiving sensory input from both the internal and external environment through nerves. Processing the input information in the central nervous system (CNS), primarily in the brain and spinal cord. Responding to stimuli by transmitting nerve impulses to effector organs such as muscles and glands for appropriate actions. Thus, all the given options are correct.

hi.question: तंत्रिका तंत्र के मूल कार्य हैं-
options: तंत्रिकाओं द्वारा आंतरिक और बाहरी वातावरण से संवेदी इनपुट प्राप्त करना
hi.explanation: तंत्रिका तंत्र निम्नलिखित मूल कार्य करता है: तंत्रिकाओं के माध्यम से आंतरिक और बाह्य दोनों पर्यावरण से संवेदी निवेश प्राप्त करना। केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) में, मुख्य रूप से मस्तिष्क और मेरुरज्जु में निवेशित सूचनाओं का प्रसंस्करण करना। उचित क्रियाओं के लिए पेशियों तथा ग्रंथियों जैसे कार्यकर अंगों तक तंत्रिका आवेगों को संचारित करके उद्दीपनों के प्रति अनुक्रिया करना। अतः, दिए गए सभी विकल्प सही हैं।

questions.question: Which of the following have a more developed neural system?
questions.explanation: The complexity of the neural system increases in the following order: Lower invertebrates (e.g., Hydra) have a simple nerve net without a central nervous system. Insects have a more organized neural system, including a brain and ganglia. Vertebrates have the most developed neural system, consisting of a highly specialized brain, spinal cord, and a complex network of nerves for rapid communication and coordination. Thus, vertebrates possess the most advanced neural system.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से किसमें अधिक विकसित तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है?
hi.explanation: तंत्रिका तंत्र की जटिलता निम्नलिखित क्रम में बढ़ती है: निम्न अकशेरुकियों (जैसे, हाइड्रा) में केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र के बिना एक सरल तंत्रिका जाल होता है। कीटों में अधिक संगठित तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है, जिसमें मस्तिष्क और गुच्छिकाएँ शामिल होती हैं। कशेरुकियों में सबसे विकसित तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है, जिसमें तीव्र संचार और समन्वय के लिए एक अत्यधिक विशिष्टीकृत मस्तिष्क, मेरुरज्जु और तंत्रिकाओं का एक जटिल जाल होता है। अतः, कशेरुकियों में सबसे उन्नत तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है।

questions.question: The human neural system is divided into
options: Three parts- CNS, PNS and ANS
Three parts- Forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain
questions.explanation: The human neural system is divided into two main parts: Central Nervous System (CNS) - Consists of the brain and spinal cord, responsible for processing and controlling information. Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) - Comprises all the nerves that connect the CNS to different parts of the body. It includes: Somatic Nervous System (voluntary control) Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) (involuntary control) Thus, the neural system is primarily divided into CNS and PNS, making option A correct.

hi.question: मानव तंत्रिका तंत्र को विभाजित किया गया है-
options: दो भागों में- CNS और PNS
दो भागों में- CNS और ANS
तीन भागों में- CNS, PNS और ANS
तीन भागों में- अग्रमस्तिष्क, मध्यमस्तिष्क और पश्चमस्तिष्क
hi.explanation: मानव तंत्रिका तंत्र दो मुख्य भागों में विभाजित है: केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) - इसमें मस्तिष्क और मेरुरज्जु शामिल हैं, जो सूचनाओं के प्रसंस्करण और नियंत्रण के लिए उत्तरदायी है। परिधीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (PNS) - इसमें वे सभी तंत्रिकाएँ शामिल हैं जो CNS को शरीर के विभिन्न भागों से जोड़ती हैं। इसमें शामिल हैं: कायिक तंत्रिका तंत्र (ऐच्छिक नियंत्रण) स्वायत्त तंत्रिका तंत्र (ANS) (अनैच्छिक नियंत्रण) अतः, तंत्रिका तंत्र मुख्य रूप से CNS और PNS में विभाजित है, जिससे विकल्प A सही है।

questions.question: Afferent nerve fibres carry impulses from
questions.explanation: Afferent nerve fibers are responsible for carrying sensory impulses from receptors (sensory organs) to the central nervous system (CNS). These impulses provide information about external and internal stimuli to the brain or spinal cord for processing. In contrast, efferent nerve fibers carry motor commands from the CNS to effectors (muscles and glands).

hi.question: अभिवाही तंत्रिका तंतु आवेगों को वहन करते हैं।
options: प्रभावी अंग से ग्राही के लिये
hi.explanation: अभिवाही तंत्रिका तंतु रिसेप्टर्स (संवेदी अंगों) से केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (सीएनएस) तक संवेदी आवेगों को ले जाने के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं। ये आवेग मस्तिष्क या रीढ़ की हड्डी को प्रसंस्करण के लिए बाहरी और आंतरिक उत्तेजनाओं के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करते हैं। इसके विपरीत, अपवाही तंत्रिका तंतु सीएनएस से प्रभावकों (मांसपेशियों और ग्रंथियों) तक मोटर कमांड ले जाते हैं।

questions.question: Visceral nervous system is the part of
questions.explanation: The visceral nervous system is a part of the peripheral nervous system (PNS). It consists of nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses that transmit impulses between the central nervous system (CNS) and visceral organs (such as the heart, lungs, intestines, etc.). It plays a crucial role in autonomic functions like digestion, respiration and circulation.

hi.question: अंतरंग तंत्रिका तंत्र निम्न का भाग है:
hi.explanation: आंत संबंधी तंत्रिका तंत्र परिधीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (PNS) का एक हिस्सा है। इसमें तंत्रिकाएँ, तंतु, गैन्ग्लिया और प्लेक्सस होते हैं जो केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) और आंत संबंधी अंगों (जैसे हृदय, फेफड़े, आंत, आदि) के बीच आवेगों को संचारित करते हैं। यह पाचन, श्वसन और परिसंचरण जैसे स्वायत्त कार्यों में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।

questions.question: Multipolar neurons are found in the
questions.explanation: Multipolar neurons have one axon and two or more dendrites and are the most common type of neurons in the human body. They are primarily found in the cerebral cortex, where they play a crucial role in higher-order brain functions such as cognition, motor control, and sensory processing. Retina of the eye (A) contains bipolar neurons (one axon and one dendrite). Embryonic stage (C) is associated with unipolar neurons, not multipolar neurons. None of the above (D) is incorrect as multipolar neurons are present in the cerebral cortex.

hi.question: बहुध्रुवीय न्यूरॉन पाए जाते हैं-

questions.question: Unmyelinated nerve fibres that do not form a myelin sheath around the axon are commonly found in _____ A _____and the _____B_____ neural systems. Fill in the blanks ( {A} and {B} ) with correct option.
questions.explanation: Unmyelinated nerve fibers are commonly found in the autonomous nervous system (ANS) and the somatic neural system. The ANS controls involuntary functions and includes sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions, where many neurons are unmyelinated. The somatic neural system contains both myelinated and unmyelinated fibers that control voluntary muscle movements.

hi.question: अनाच्चादी तंत्रिका तंतु जो तंत्रिकाक्ष के चारों ओर एक माइलिन आच्छद नहीं बनाते हैं, आमतौर पर .......... A .......... और .......... B .......... तंत्रिका तंत्र में पाए जाते हैं।रिक्त स्थान (A और B) को सही विकल्प से भरें।

questions.question: In resting stage, the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to __________A_________ ions and nearly impermeable to_________B_________. Fill in the blanks ( {A} and {B} ) with correct option
questions.explanation: During the resting stage of a neuron: The axonal membrane is more permeable to potassium (K⁺) ions, allowing them to move freely. The membrane is nearly impermeable to sodium (Na⁺) ions, preventing their free movement. This selective permeability is maintained by the sodium-potassium pump, which actively transports 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in, helping maintain the resting membrane potential (-70 mV).

questions.question: When the neuron is resting, the axonal membrane is................ to negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm
questions.explanation: During the resting stage, the axonal membrane is impermeable to negatively charged proteins present inside the axoplasm. These proteins contribute to the negative charge inside the neuron, helping establish the resting membrane potential (-70 mV). Additionally: The membrane is selectively permeable to K⁺ (potassium) ions, allowing them to move out. It is nearly impermeable to Na⁺ (sodium) ions, preventing their inward movement. The sodium-potassium pump actively maintains the resting potential by exchanging 3 Na⁺ out for 2 K⁺ in.

hi.question: जब न्यूरॉन विश्राम अवस्था में होता है, तो तंत्रिकाक्ष झिल्ली अक्षद्रव्य में मौजूद ऋणात्मक रूप से आवेशित प्रोटीनों के लिए ................. होती है

questions.question: The electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane when concentration of {K}^{+} is high inside the axon and low outside, it is known as
questions.explanation: During the resting state of a neuron, the concentration of K⁺ (potassium) ions is high inside the axon and low outside, while Na⁺ (sodium) ions are high outside and low inside. This results in an electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane, known as the resting potential (~ -70mV). The sodium-potassium pump helps maintain this potential by actively transporting 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in. Other options: Action potential (A) occurs when there is a rapid change in membrane potential due to Na⁺ influx. Refractory potential (C) refers to the period after an action potential when the neuron cannot generate another impulse immediately. All of the above (D) is incorrect as only resting potential fits the given condition.

hi.question: जब {K}^{+} की सांद्रता तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंदर अधिक और बाहर कम होती है, तो प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के पार विद्युत विभव अंतर को कहा जाता है-

questions.question: A wave of action potential is termed as
questions.explanation: A wave of action potential propagating along the neuron is known as a nerve impulse. This impulse is generated due to the depolarization and repolarization of the neuron membrane, allowing electrical signals to be transmitted. Sensory impulse (A) refers to signals transmitted by sensory neurons to the central nervous system. Activation impulse (C) is not a standard term in neurophysiology. Motor impulse (D) refers to signals carried by motor neurons to muscles or glands, but the general term for an action potential wave is nerve impulse.

hi.question: क्रियात्मक विभव की एक तरंग को कहा जाता है

questions.question: Maintenance of the ionic gradients across the resting membrane is done by
questions.explanation: The ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by the sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ pump), which actively transports: 3 Na⁺ ions out of the neuron 2 K⁺ ions in This process requires ATP and is an example of active transport of ions to maintain the resting membrane potential (-70mV). Passive transport of ions (B) does not require energy and occurs through diffusion, but the maintenance of gradients requires active transport. Active/passive transport of neurotransmitters (C & D) are involved in synaptic transmission, not in maintaining resting potential.

hi.question: विश्राम झिल्ली के पार आयनिक प्रवणताओं का रखरखाव किसके द्वारा किया जाता है?

questions.question: For the maintenance of ionic gradients across the resting membrane, the sodium-potassium pump transports
questions.explanation: The sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ pump) is responsible for maintaining the resting membrane potential by actively transporting: 3 Na⁺ (sodium) ions out of the neuron 2 K⁺ (potassium) ions into the neuron This process: Requires ATP (active transport) Helps in maintaining the ionic gradient Keeps the inside of the neuron negatively charged compared to the outside Other options are incorrect because they do not reflect the correct direction and ratio of ion transport.

hi.question: विश्राम झिल्ली के पार आयनिक प्रवणताओं के रखरखाव के लिए, सोडियम-पोटेशियम पंप परिवहन करता है-
options: 3Na+ बाहर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका में।
2Na+ बाहर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका में।
3Na+ अंदर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका से बाहर।
2Na+ अंदर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका से बाहर

questions.question: In the resting stage of a neuron, concentration gradient generates due to
options: High concentration of {K}^{+} and low concentration of {Na}^{+} inside the axon
High concentration of {Na}^{+} and low concentration of {K}^{+} inside the axon
Low concentration of {Na}^{+} outside the axon
High concentration of {K}^{+} outside the axon
questions.explanation: During the resting stage of a neuron, the concentration gradient is maintained by the sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ pump), which actively transports: 3 Na⁺ out of the neuron 2 K⁺ in to the neuron As a result: Inside the axon: High K⁺, Low Na⁺ Outside the axon: High Na⁺, Low K⁺ This ionic gradient helps maintain the resting membrane potential (-70 mV), making the inside of the neuron negatively charged compared to the outside.

options: तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंदर {K}^{+} की उच्च सांद्रता और {Na}^{+} की निम्न सांद्रता

questions.question: During the transmission of nerve impulse through a nerve fibre, the potential on the inner side of the plasma membrane has ............... type of electric charge
options: First +ve then -ve and continue to be -ve
First +ve then -ve and again back to +ve
First -ve then +ve and again back to -ve
questions.explanation: During the transmission of a nerve impulse, the electric charge on the inner side of the plasma membrane undergoes the following changes: Resting potential (-ve inside): The inner side of the neuron membrane is negatively charged, and the outer side is positively charged due to the high concentration of K⁺ inside and Na⁺ outside. Depolarization (+ve inside): When an action potential is generated, Na⁺ ions rush into the neuron, making the inner side positively charged and the outer side negative. Repolarization (-ve inside again): K⁺ ions move out, restoring the negative charge inside the neuron and the positive charge outside. Thus, the sequence of changes is:Negative (-ve) → Positive (+ve) → Negative (-ve) again, which matches option (D).

questions.question: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, the action potential results from the movement of
options: {K}^{+} ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid.
{Na}^{+} ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid.
{K}^{+} ions from extracellular fluid to intra cellular fluid.
{Na}^{+} ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid.
questions.explanation: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, an action potential is generated due to the influx of Na⁺ ions into the neuron. At resting potential (-70 mV): The neuron is more negative inside due to a high concentration of K⁺ inside and Na⁺ outside. During depolarization (Action potential): Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open, allowing Na⁺ ions to rush into the intracellular fluid. This makes the inside of the neuron positively charged compared to the outside. Repolarization: K⁺ channels open, and K⁺ moves out, restoring the negative charge inside the neuron. Thus, the movement of Na⁺ ions from extracellular to intracellular fluid is responsible for generating the action potential.

questions.explanation: The ionic gradient across the resting membrane is primarily maintained by the sodium-potassium pump. This pump actively transports sodium ions out of the cell and potassium ions into the cell, creating and maintaining the concentration differences across the membrane.

options: there is a rapid influx of {K}^{+} at that site.
there is a rapid efflux of {Na}^{+} at that site.
there is a rapid influx of {Na}^{+} at that site.
there is a rapid efflux of {K}^{+} at that site.
questions.explanation: When a stimulus is applied to the axonal membrane, it causes depolarization by opening voltage-gated Na⁺ channels, leading to: Rapid influx of Na⁺ ions into the neuron. The inside of the membrane becomes positively charged compared to the outside. This change in charge triggers an action potential, allowing the nerve impulse to propagate. Efflux of Na⁺ (Option B) does not occur during depolarization. Influx or efflux of K⁺ (Options A & D) happens during repolarization, not at the start of the action potential.

questions.question: An action potential in the nerve fibre is produced when positive and negative charges on the outside and the inside of the axon membrane are reversed, because
options: More potassium ions enter the axon as compared to sodium ions leaving it
More sodium ions enter the axon as compared to potassium ions leaving it
All potassium ions leave the axon
All sodium ions enter the axon
questions.explanation: An action potential occurs when the membrane potential is reversed, making the inside of the axon temporarily positive compared to the outside. This happens due to: Depolarization Phase: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open, allowing Na⁺ to rush into the axon. This causes the inside to become more positive, reversing the normal resting charge. Repolarization Phase: K⁺ channels open, allowing K⁺ to leave the axon, restoring the negative charge inside. Thus, more Na⁺ enters the axon than K⁺ leaves, leading to the reversal of charge, which is the basis of the action potential. Why other options are incorrect: (A) More potassium ions enter the axon → Incorrect, because K⁺ exits the axon during repolarization. (C) All potassium ions leave the axon → Incorrect, as not all K⁺ leaves, only enough to restore resting potential. (D) All sodium ions enter the axon → Incorrect, as Na⁺ entry is controlled and stops after depolarization. Thus, the correct answer is (B).

hi.question: जब एक उत्तेजना ध्रुवीकृत झिल्ली पर एक साइट पर लागू होती है तो यह .................. आयन के लिए स्वतंत्र रूप से पारगम्य हो जाती है

questions.question: Nerve fibres transmit the nerve message by ................... means.
questions.explanation: Nerve fibers transmit nerve impulses through an electrochemical process, which involves both electrical and chemical components: Electrical transmission (Within the neuron): Action potentials propagate along the neuron due to ion movement (Na⁺ and K⁺) across the membrane. This electrical impulse moves from one end of the neuron to the other. Chemical transmission (At synapses): When the impulse reaches the synapse, neurotransmitters (e.g., acetylcholine, dopamine) are released to transmit the signal to the next neuron. Why other options are incorrect: (A) Chemical → Incorrect, as only synaptic transmission is chemical, but impulse propagation along the neuron is electrical. (B) Physical → Incorrect, as no physical movement or mechanical force is involved. (D) Electrical → Partially correct, but it ignores the role of chemical neurotransmitters at the synapse. Thus, nerve impulse transmission is best described as electrochemical.

hi.question: तंत्रिका तंतु .............. माध्यम से तंत्रिका संदेश को संचारित करते हैं।

questions.question: The junction between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next is called
questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next neuron. It serves as the communication point where nerve impulses are transmitted from one neuron to another. There are two types of synapses: Chemical synapse: Uses neurotransmitters (e.g., acetylcholine, dopamine) to transmit signals. The impulse is converted from an electrical to a chemical signal at the synaptic cleft. Electrical synapse: Allows direct ion flow between neurons through gap junctions, leading to faster transmission. Why other options are incorrect: (A) Constant bridge → Incorrect, as synapses are not permanent physical bridges; they involve chemical signaling. (B) Junction point → Vague term, not the specific biological term. (C) Joint → Incorrect, as joints are connections between bones, not neurons. Thus, the correct term for the neuron-to-neuron connection is synapse.

hi.question: एक न्यूरॉन के तंत्रिकाक्ष और अगले के द्रुमिका के बीच के जंक्शन को कहा जाता है-

questions.question: A synapse is formed by
questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction between two neurons where nerve impulse transmission occurs. It consists of: Pre-synaptic membrane (A) This is the axon terminal of the transmitting neuron. It releases neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. Post-synaptic membrane (B) This is the dendritic membrane of the receiving neuron. It contains receptor proteins that bind to neurotransmitters, allowing signal transmission. Synaptic cleft (C) A small gap between the pre- and post-synaptic membranes. Neurotransmitters diffuse across this space to transmit the impulse. Since a synapse is composed of all three components, the correct answer is (D) All of the above.

questions.question: The receptors of neurotransmitters are present on/in the
questions.explanation: Neurotransmitter receptors are located on the post-synaptic membrane, where they bind to neurotransmitters to propagate nerve impulses.

questions.question: Which of the following act is responsible for the depolarisation of the neuron?
questions.explanation: Depolarization is the process where the inside of the neuron becomes less negative compared to the outside. This occurs when: A stimulus triggers the opening of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels. Na⁺ ions rush into the neuron, making the inside more positive (from -70 mV to around +40 mV). This generates an action potential, allowing the nerve impulse to propagate. Why other options are incorrect: (A) Opening of voltage-gated K⁺ channel → Incorrect, as this happens during repolarization, not depolarization. (C) Closure of voltage-gated K⁺ channel → Incorrect, K⁺ channels remain closed during depolarization but open later for repolarization. (D) Closure of voltage-gated Na⁺ channel → Incorrect, as depolarization requires Na⁺ channels to be open for Na⁺ influx. Thus, the opening of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels is responsible for depolarization.

hi.question: न्यूरॉन के विध्रुवण के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कार्य उत्तरदायी है?

questions.question: If the inside of membrane becomes more negative, it leads to
questions.explanation: Hyperpolarisation occurs when the inside of the neuron becomes more negative than the resting membrane potential (-70 mV). This happens when excess K⁺ exits the neuron or Cl⁻ enters, making the potential more negative than -70 mV, sometimes reaching -90 mV. This phase follows repolarisation and prevents immediate reactivation of the neuron (refractory period). Why other options are incorrect: (A) Depolarisation → Incorrect, as depolarization makes the inside more positive due to Na⁺ influx. (B) Repolarisation → Incorrect, as repolarization restores the original negative charge after depolarization. (D) Polarisation → Incorrect, as it refers to the resting state (-70 mV), not increased negativity. Thus, if the inside of the membrane becomes more negative, it leads to hyperpolarisation.

hi.question: यदि झिल्ली के अंदर का भाग अधिक ऋणात्मक हो जाता है, तो यह होता है-

questions.question: Suppose the terminal ends of axon are in contact with dendrites of four adjacent neurons, the nerve impulse of the axon will
options: Travel in all the four neurons
Get distributed in all the four neurons resulting in a weak impulse
Travel only in one neuron which is in closest contact and with the same intensity
Travel in none of the neurons because the impulse travels from dendrites of one neuron into the axon of another neuron
questions.explanation: When the axon terminal of a neuron is in contact with the dendrites of multiple adjacent neurons, the nerve impulse is transmitted to all of them through synaptic connections. The impulse does not weaken as it follows the "all-or-none law", meaning if a neuron is stimulated beyond its threshold, it will fire at full strength. Synapses distribute the impulse to all connected neurons simultaneously. The transmission is facilitated by neurotransmitters, which allow the signal to be carried to multiple neurons. Why other options are incorrect: (B) Impulse gets distributed, resulting in a weak impulse → Incorrect, because the impulse remains the same strength in each neuron. (C) Travels only in one neuron in closest contact → Incorrect, because synapses allow the impulse to reach all connected neurons. (D) Travels in none of the neurons → Incorrect, as impulses always travel from axon terminals to dendrites across synapses. Thus, the impulse will be transmitted to all four neurons.

questions.question: During depolarisation, the outer surface of the membrane becomes
questions.explanation: During depolarization, the neuron undergoes a temporary reversal of charges due to the influx of Na⁺ ions into the axoplasm. In the resting state, the outer surface is positively charged due to a high concentration of Na⁺ outside the neuron. When depolarization occurs, voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open, allowing Na⁺ to rush into the neuron. This causes the inside of the neuron to become positive while the outer surface becomes negatively charged. Why other options are incorrect: (B) Positively charged → Incorrect, as the outer surface becomes negative during depolarization. (C) Neutrally charged → Incorrect, as a charge difference still exists across the membrane. (D) None of the above → Incorrect, since option (A) is correct. Thus, during depolarization, the outer surface of the membrane becomes negatively charged.

hi.question: विध्रुवण के दौरान, झिल्ली की बाहरी सतह हो जाती है-

questions.question: When an impulse arrives at axon terminal, it stimulates synaptic vesicle to move towards the membrane, where they fuse with plasma membrane and release their neurotransmitter in
questions.explanation: When a nerve impulse reaches the axon terminal, the following sequence occurs: Ca²⁺ influx → Voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels open, allowing calcium ions to enter the axon terminal. Synaptic vesicles move toward the pre-synaptic membrane and fuse with it. Neurotransmitters (e.g., acetylcholine, dopamine) are released into the synaptic cleft via exocytosis. The neurotransmitters diffuse across the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the post-synaptic membrane, triggering an action potential in the next neuron. Why other options are incorrect: (A) Receptor → Incorrect, as neurotransmitters are released into the synaptic cleft first before binding to receptors. (B) Pre-synaptic membrane → Incorrect, because the neurotransmitters are released from this membrane, not into it. (D) Post-synaptic membrane → Incorrect, as neurotransmitters reach the post-synaptic membrane after diffusing through the synaptic cleft. Thus, neurotransmitters are released into the synaptic cleft, making option (C) correct.

hi.question: जब कोई आवेग अक्षतंतु के अंतिम सिरे पर पहुँचता है, तो यह सिनेप्टिक पुटिकाओं को झिल्ली की ओर गति करने के लिए उद्दीपित करता है, जहाँ वे प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के साथ संगलित हो जाती हैं और अपने न्यूरोट्रांसमीटर को ________ में मुक्त करती हैं।

questions.question: The new potential developed in post-synaptic neuron after allowing entry of ions is
questions.explanation: ✔ The post-synaptic potential can be excitatory (EPSP) or inhibitory (IPSP) depending on the neurotransmitter and ion channels activated. ✘ A (Always inhibitory) and B (Always excitatory) → Incorrect, as it depends on the type of synapse.✘ D (Neither excitatory nor inhibitory) → Incorrect, as synaptic potentials always fall into one of these categories.

questions.question: Which of the following meninx is in contact with the brain tissue?
options: No meninx is in contact with the brain tissue
questions.explanation: The brain is covered by three protective membranes called meninges: Dura mater – The outermost, tough layer. Arachnoid mater – The middle, web-like layer. Pia mater – The innermost layer, which is thin and directly in contact with the brain tissue. It closely adheres to the surface of the brain and spinal cord, providing protection and nourishment.

questions.question: All of the following are parts of forebrain, except
questions.explanation: The forebrain consists of: Cerebrum (including association areas) Thalamus Hypothalamus Corpus callosum (which connects the two cerebral hemispheres) The cerebellum, however, is a part of the hindbrain, not the forebrain. It is responsible for coordinating movement, posture, and balance.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित सभी अग्र मस्तिष्क के भाग हैं, सिवाय-

questions.question: The association areas are present in the
questions.explanation: Association areas are regions in the cerebral cortex responsible for integrating sensory and motor information. They play a key role in complex cognitive functions such as memory, reasoning, learning, and decision-making. Corpus callosum is a bundle of nerve fibers that connects the two cerebral hemispheres. Amygdala is part of the limbic system involved in emotions. Hypothalamus regulates homeostasis, hunger, thirst, and hormone secretion.

hi.question: सहभागी क्षेत्र ________ में उपस्थित होते हैं।

questions.question: The association areas are not responsible for:
questions.explanation: Association areas of the cerebral cortex are involved in intersensory associations, communication, and memory. These regions help integrate sensory information, facilitate reasoning, and enable higher cognitive functions. Regulation of sexual behaviour is controlled by the hypothalamus, not the association areas of the cerebral cortex. The hypothalamus influences sexual drive, hormonal regulation, and reproductive behavior through neuroendocrine control.

hi.question: सहचारी क्षेत्र ______ के लिए उत्तरदायी नहीं हैं:

questions.question: The limbic system is formed by
questions.explanation: The limbic system is a complex network of brain structures involved in emotions, memory, and motivation. It consists of: Hypothalamus – Regulates emotions, hunger, thirst, and hormonal control. Amygdala – Plays a key role in emotional processing, fear response, and memory. Hippocampus – Involved in learning and memory formation. Other structures like the thalamus and parts of the cerebrum also contribute to limbic functions.

hi.question: लिम्बिक तंत्र किसके द्बवारा बना होता है?

questions.question: Which one of the following is the primary function of occipital lobe?
questions.explanation: The occipital lobe is the primary visual processing center of the brain. It is responsible for receiving and interpreting visual information from the retina via the optic nerves. Regulation of the hunger drive is controlled by the hypothalamus. Regulation of the sleep cycle is managed by the hypothalamus and brainstem. Reception of touch senses is handled by the parietal lobe.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा पश्चकपाल पालि का प्राथमिक कार्य है?

questions.question: Which part of the brain is like a defense castle controlling moods and plays an important role in emotional behaviour, such as aggression and remembering fear?
questions.explanation: The amygdala is a key structure of the limbic system that plays a crucial role in processing emotions, especially fear, aggression, and mood regulation. It helps in forming emotional memories, particularly those related to threats and danger, making it essential for survival. Hippocampus is mainly responsible for learning and memory formation. Limbic system is a broader system that includes the amygdala, hippocampus, and hypothalamus, which collectively regulate emotions and memory. Thalamus acts as a relay station for sensory information but does not directly control emotions like fear and aggression.

questions.question: The outermost layer of the 3 cranial meninges is
questions.explanation: The three cranial meninges that protect the brain are: Dura mater – The outermost, tough, and thick fibrous layer that provides structural support. Arachnoid mater – The middle layer, web-like in structure, involved in cerebrospinal fluid circulation. Pia mater – The innermost, delicate layer that is in direct contact with the brain tissue. Sclera is not a meninge; it is the outer white layer of the eye.

questions.question: Hypothalamus controls I. Urge for eating and drinking II. Thermoregulation III. Hormones production that regulates the secretion of pituitary gland IV. Creative thinking and consciousness
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus plays a crucial role in: Urge for eating and drinking – It regulates hunger and thirst via the feeding and satiety centers. Thermoregulation – It controls body temperature by signaling mechanisms like sweating and shivering. Hormone production that regulates the secretion of the pituitary gland – It releases releasing and inhibiting hormones that control the pituitary gland, influencing metabolism, growth, and stress response. Incorrect statement: Creative thinking and consciousness – This function is regulated by the cerebrum, particularly the prefrontal cortex, not the hypothalamus. Thus, statements I, II, and III are correct, while statement IV is incorrect.

questions.question: Choose the correct option about {Na}^{+}-{K}^{+} pump I. Needs energy (ATP) to work II. Expels 3 {Na}^{+} for every 2 {~K}^{+} ions imported III. Works against a concentration gradient IV. Maintains a resting potential
options: Only II and III are correct
Only I and III are correct
None of the above is correct
questions.explanation: The Na⁺ – K⁺ pump is an active transport mechanism that maintains the resting membrane potential by: Needs energy (ATP) to work (Statement I) The pump uses ATP to transport ions against their concentration gradient. Expels 3 Na⁺ for every 2 K⁺ imported (Statement II) It pumps 3 Na⁺ out of the neuron and 2 K⁺ in, keeping the inside negative. Works against a concentration gradient (Statement III) The pump moves Na⁺ out (where it is already high) and K⁺ in (where it is already high), which requires energy. Maintains a resting potential (Statement IV) By keeping Na⁺ out and K⁺ in, it helps maintain the resting membrane potential (~ -70mV). Since all statements are correct, option (A) is the correct choice.

questions.question: The electrical potential difference across the depolarised membrane is called the
questions.explanation: When a neuron is stimulated, its membrane undergoes depolarization, causing a rapid influx of Na⁺ ions. This results in an electrical potential difference across the membrane, known as the action potential (~+40 mV). The action potential allows the nerve impulse to propagate along the neuron. Why other options are incorrect: Resting potential (B): Occurs when the neuron is not conducting an impulse (~ -70 mV). Water potential (C) & Solute potential (D): These terms are related to osmosis and plant physiology, not neural activity. Thus, the electrical potential difference during depolarization is called the action potential.

questions.question: In a nerve, if sodium pump is blocked, which of the following is most likely to happen?
options: {Na}^{+} and {K}^{+} will increase outside the cell
questions.explanation: The sodium-potassium (Na⁺/K⁺) pump actively transports: 3 Na⁺ out of the neuron 2 K⁺ in to the neuron This maintains the resting membrane potential (-70mV) and keeps Na⁺ concentration higher outside and K⁺ concentration higher inside. If the sodium pump is blocked: Na⁺ will not be pumped out and will accumulate inside the neuron. K⁺ will not be transported in, but it will still diffuse out through leak channels. This will disrupt the ionic balance, leading to continuous depolarization and loss of resting potential. Why other options are incorrect: (A) Na⁺ and K⁺ will increase outside the cell → Incorrect, because Na⁺ will increase inside, and K⁺ will leak out but not increase outside. (B) Na⁺ outside the nerve will increase → Incorrect, as Na⁺ will accumulate inside instead. (D) K⁺ inside the nerve will increase → Incorrect, because K⁺ will not be pumped in and may even leak out.

questions.question: The charge on the outer side of neuron at resting is
questions.explanation: During the resting state of a neuron, the charge distribution across the membrane is: Inside the neuron → Negative due to the presence of large negatively charged proteins and high K⁺ concentration. Outside the neuron → Positive due to the high concentration of Na⁺ ions. This charge difference is maintained by the sodium-potassium pump, which actively transports: 3 Na⁺ out of the neuron 2 K⁺ in to the neuron This creates the resting membrane potential (~ -70 mV) with the outside being positive relative to the inside. Why other options are incorrect: (B) Negative → Incorrect, as the inside is negative, not the outside. (C) Zero → Incorrect, because there is a measurable potential difference (~ -70 mV). (D) Alternate, negative and positive → Incorrect, as alternation occurs only during action potential propagation, not at rest.

questions.question: During conduction of nerve impulse, when stimulus is applied
questions.explanation: During the conduction of a nerve impulse, when a stimulus is applied, the following events occur: Depolarization: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open, allowing Na⁺ ions to rush into the axoplasm (inside the neuron). This causes the inside of the neuron to become positively charged, leading to the generation of an action potential. Repolarization: K⁺ channels open, allowing K⁺ to move out of the axoplasm, restoring the negative charge inside the neuron. Why other options are incorrect: (A) Na⁺ moves out of axoplasm → Incorrect, as Na⁺ enters the neuron during depolarization. (C) K⁺ moves into axoplasm → Incorrect, as K⁺ moves out during repolarization. (D) Ca²⁺ moves into axoplasm → Incorrect, as Ca²⁺ is involved in neurotransmitter release at synapses, not in action potential conduction.
